question.text: Two bodies travel along the same linear path. At time t = 0, both pass through a fixed point A simultaneously. At this instant, the first body possesses a speed 2u and a uniform acceleration a, while the second body possesses a speed u and a uniform acceleration 2a in the same direction. Determine the distance covered by the bodies from point A up to the moment when one catches up with the other.
conditions: motion along the same straight line
both bodies pass point A at time t = 0
first body has initial speed 2u and constant acceleration a
second body has initial speed u and constant acceleration 2a

solution.approach: Write the position of each object from point A as a function of time and set them equal at the overtaking instant.

steps.text: Write the position of the first object (initial velocity 2u, acceleration a) from A.
Write the position of the second object (initial velocity u, acceleration 2a) from A.
Set the positions equal at the overtaking time and solve for t.
steps.equation: 2ut + ½at² = ut + at² → ut = ½at² → t = 2u/a

steps.text: Substitute t = 2u/a into the first object's position to get the distance moved.
